title: MA 16100 or MA 16500 (Plane Analytic Geometry And Calculus I)
description: A first calculus course: limits, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integrals, in versions with more or less review.
notes: Choice slot: Purdue's MA 16100 (5 credits) or MA 16500 (4 credits). Official descriptions are in data/raw/purdue/courses/.

title: Written Communication
description: A first-year writing course on academic reading, argument, research, and revision.

title: Free Elective
description: Any course the student chooses.

title: MA 16200 or MA 16600 (Plane Analytic Geometry And Calculus II)
description: A second calculus course: techniques of integration, sequences and series, and vectors.
notes: Choice slot: Purdue's MA 16200 or MA 16600. Official descriptions are in data/raw/purdue/courses/.

title: AI Working Competency
description: A short course, or part of a course, that builds working knowledge of artificial intelligence tools: what they can do, their limits, and their responsible use.

title: Language and Culture I
description: A world language course or an approved course on another culture.

title: MA 26100 or MA 27101 (Multivariate Calculus)
description: A course in multivariable calculus: partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus, in a regular or honors version.
notes: Choice slot: Purdue's MA 26100 or MA 27101 (honors). Official descriptions are in data/raw/purdue/courses/.

title: Language and Culture II
description: A second world language or culture course.

title: MA 26500 or MA 35100 (Linear Algebra)
description: A first course in linear algebra: systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, determinants, and eigenvalues.
notes: Choice slot: Purdue's MA 26500 or MA 35100. Official descriptions are in data/raw/purdue/courses/.

title: Technical Writing and Presentation
description: A course in communicating scientific and technical information in writing and in oral presentations.

title: Language and Culture III
description: A third world language or culture course.

title: Science, Technology and Society
description: A course on how science and technology interact with society, ethics, and public policy.

title: STAT 35000 or STAT 51100 (Introduction To Statistics)
description: An introductory statistics course: data analysis, probability, sampling distributions, estimation, and hypothesis testing.
notes: Choice slot: Purdue's STAT 35000 or STAT 51100. Official descriptions are in data/raw/purdue/courses/.

title: CS Track Course
description: An upper-level computer science course required by, or chosen from, the student's track, such as software engineering, security, machine intelligence, or systems software.
notes: Purdue: six or seven track courses.

title: General Education I
description: A general education course in the humanities or social sciences.

title: Great Issues in Science
description: A course on major issues at the intersection of science and society, often team-taught across disciplines.

title: General Education II
description: A second general education course in the humanities or social sciences.

title: General Education III
description: A third general education course in the humanities or social sciences.

title: Lab Science I
description: A laboratory science course outside computer science, such as biology, chemistry, or physics.

title: Lab Science II
description: A second laboratory science course.
